title: Cap. 1 subject: Tertio — rationality as common condition
pass_a_gloss: III. In the third place let us now approach the qualities or conditions of the subject considered commonly and indistinctly; that is, unto inquiring by what qualities it is necessary that that subject be clothed, and as it were invested, into which this Divine act either of predestination or of reprobation is indiscriminately terminated. First, it is outside controversy that, in order that the act of predestination or reprobation fall upon any subject whatsoever, this quality or condition is required, that that subject be endowed with a rational nature. Rationality therefore is a necessary condition always to be supposed in the subject either predestined or reprobated. Ready at hand and obvious to anyone is the reason of this matter; because namely both predestination and reprobation is a decree of God concerning the supernatural end of eternal beatitude; of which end a brute nature can in no way be capable. When therefore we say someone ordered unto beatitude through predestination, or excluded from beatitude through reprobation, it is necessary that both be understood of a rational creature. But things that are clear ought not to be long.
pass_b_english: III. Third: the qualities or conditions of the subject taken commonly and without distinction — what must clothe that subject on which the Divine act of predestination or reprobation, taken without discrimination, terminates. First, beyond dispute: for either act to fall on any subject at all, that subject must be endowed with a rational nature. Rationality is therefore a necessary condition always to be supposed in the predestined or the reprobate. The reason is plain to anyone. Both predestination and reprobation are God's decree about the supernatural end of eternal blessedness, and brute nature cannot be capable of that end. So when we say someone is ordered to blessedness by predestination, or shut out of it by reprobation, both must be understood of a rational creature. What is clear need not be long.
source_text: III. Tertio in loco jam accedamus ad qualitates sive conditiones subjecti communiter & indistincte considerati; hoc est, ad inquirendum, quibus qualitatibus necesse sit ut vestiatur, & quasi induatur illud subjectum, in quod hic actus Divinus sive praedestinationis sive reprobationis indiscriminatim terminetur. Primo, extra controversiam est, ut actus praedestinationis aut reprobationis cadat in subjectum quodcunque, hanc qualitatem sive conditionem requiri, ut illud subjectum sit natura rationali praeditum. Rationalitas ergo est necessaria conditio semper supponenda in subjecto vel praedestinato, vel reprobato. In promptu & cuivis obvia est hujus rei ratio; quia scilicet tam praedestinatio quam reprobatio est decretum Dei circa finem supernaturalem aeternae beatitudinis; cujus finis natura bruta nullo modo capax esse potest. Quando igitur dicimus aliquem ad beatitudinem ordinatum per praedestinationem, aut a beatitudine exclusum per reprobationem, necesse est ut utrumque de rationali creatura intelligatur. Sed quae perspicua sunt, longa esse non debent.
